claims.text: Event replay rebuilds an aggregate's state by applying its stored events again, in stored order, to an empty instance; in the sample InMemoryEventStore.Load does it with EventSourcedOrder.FromEvents each time it loads an order.
claims.source_hint: glossary event-replay; examples/don-hang @ stage-3: EventSourcedOrder.cs:51-63, InMemoryEventStore.cs Load

claims.text: InMemoryEventStore.Load(orderId) is EventSourcedOrder.FromEvents(ReadStream(orderId)); ReadStream with the default afterVersion 0 returns the whole stream, oldest first.
FromEvents creates an order with the private constructor (Status "", Version 0) and calls Apply for each event in the sequence, in order; it calls no Pay, Cancel or Ship and does not call Record.

Apply switches on the event's type: OrderPlaced sets Id, CustomerId, TotalVnd and Status new; OrderPaid sets paid; OrderShipped sets shipped; OrderCancelled sets cancelled; then Version++. It checks no previous status and throws nothing.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: EventSourcedOrder.cs:95-121; C# docs: switch statement, type pattern

claims.text: Replaying placed, paid, cancelled for order 5 gives Status cancelled at Version 3.
Replay leaves newEvents empty, so InMemoryEventStore.Save right after Load appends nothing: Append(order.Id, LoadedVersion = Version - 0, []) passes the version check and AddRange adds no event.

Ship throws InvalidOperationException when Status is not paid, before calling Record, so a cancelled order records nothing (NewEvents stays empty), as Ship_CancelledOrder_ThrowsAndRecordsNothing asserts.
In the sample, newEvents is filled only by Record, which only Place, Pay, Cancel and Ship call, each after its rule (Place has none); so an OrderShipped enters new events only through Ship().
Enumerable.Take(2) returns the first two elements of the sequence, so FromEvents(stream.Take(2)) replays OrderPlaced and OrderPaid only and gives Status paid.
At stage-2 the real Order's Cancel had no paid check and overwrote orders.status (paid with cancelled); the row kept no earlier status.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: DonHang.Domain/Entities.cs Cancel (lines 83-88); outline item 4

claims.text: scripts/design/event-sourcing.sh runs dotnet run --project samples/DonHang.Samples -- event-sourcing on the host, no containers; output starts with order 5's stream (v1 OrderPlaced 09:00, v2 OrderPaid 09:30), then '== replayed: order 5 is paid at version 2', printed before the cancel is appended.
Nothing in the replay path (Load, ReadStream, FromEvents, Apply) sends a message or calls RabbitMQ; the sample project has no broker code in this path.

Keep rule checks in the method that records an event and keep Apply free of checks when, as in the sample's store, events are never changed or deleted: an Apply that threw on a stored event would refuse that order on every later load.
claims.source_hint: outline items 2-3, misconceptions 1 and 3; EventSourcedOrder.cs:95-98 comment

claims.text: An order loaded by replay remembers the version it was loaded at (LoadedVersion = Version minus new events), and Save passes it to Append, which refuses when the stream's count differs.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: EventSourcedOrder.cs LoadedVersion; InMemoryEventStore.cs Append, Save

claims.text: In the sample, loading from a snapshot plus the later events gives the same order as a full replay.
The real Order's constructor throws ArgumentException on invalid input, before the order exists.
